verses.text: Before anything got started, the Word already was. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The Word was already there with God from jump.
Everything that exists came through him. Nothing got made without him.
Life was in him, and that life lit up humanity.
That light keeps shining in the dark, and darkness couldn’t shut it down. ✨
God sent a man named John onto the scene.
He came as a witness, speaking up about the light so everyone could believe through him.
John wasn’t the light, though. He came to point people to it.
The real light—the one shining on everyone—was coming into the world.
He was already in the world. The world came through him, but didn’t even recognize him.
He came to his own people, and they didn’t welcome him in.
But everyone who welcomed him, everyone trusting in his name, got the right to become God’s children.
They weren’t born from bloodline, human craving, or somebody’s plan; their birth came from God.
The Word became human and set up home among us. We saw his glory—the glory of the Father’s one and only Son, full of grace and truth.
John spoke up about him, calling out, “This is the one I meant when I said, ‘The one coming after me ranks ahead of me, because he was here before me.’”
Out of all that fullness, we’ve all received grace on top of grace.
Moses brought the Law, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God—not once. The one and only Son, close to the Father’s heart, has made him known.
Here’s how John’s testimony went: Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He said it straight and didn’t deny it: “I am not the Christ.”
They pressed him: “Okay, then who? Elijah?” He said, “No.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
They said, “So who are you? We need a straight answer for the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I’m a voice calling out in the wilderness: ‘Make the Lord’s road straight,’ just like Isaiah the prophet said.”
The people who had been sent were Pharisees.
They pressed him, “Then why are you baptizing if you’re not the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet?”
John answered, “I baptize with water. But there’s someone standing right among you whom you don’t know.
He’s the one coming after me, but he ranks ahead of me. I’m not even worthy to untie his sandal strap.”
This all happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
Next day, John saw Jesus coming his way and said, “Look—the Lamb of God, the one who takes away the world’s sin!
This is the one I meant when I said, ‘A man’s coming after me, but he ranks ahead of me because he was here before me.’
I didn’t know who he was, but I came baptizing with water so he could be revealed to Israel.”
John testified, “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and stay on him.
I didn’t know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said, ‘The one you see the Spirit come down and remain on is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’
I’ve seen it, and I’m telling you: this is the Son of God.”
Next day, John was back there with two of his disciples.
He saw Jesus walking by and said, “Look—the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him and started following Jesus.
Jesus turned, saw them following, and asked, “What are you looking for?” They said, “Rabbi”—that means Teacher—“where are you staying?”
He said, “Come and see.” They went, saw where he was staying, and hung out with him that day. It was about four in the afternoon.
One of those two who heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew went straight to find his brother Simon and told him, “We found the Messiah!” (That means Christ.)
He brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You’re Simon, Jonah’s son. You’ll be called Cephas”—which means Peter.
Next day, Jesus decided to head for Galilee. He found Philip and said, “Follow me.”
Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We found the one Moses wrote about in the Law—and the prophets too: Jesus from Nazareth, Joseph’s son.”
Nathanael said, “Nazareth? Anything good really come from there?” Philip said, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming and said, “Here’s a real Israelite—no fake in him!”
Nathanael asked, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered, “I saw you under the fig tree before Philip even called you.”
Nathanael said, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are Israel’s King!”
Jesus answered, “You believe because I said I saw you under the fig tree? You’re about to see way greater things than that!”
Then he said, “I’m telling you the truth: you’ll see heaven opened and God’s angels going up and down on the Son of Man.” 🌌
